The trade tests that the priced hike path will not be delivered in full.

Energy-constrained global easing (desk thesis) is the main regime difference that can keep AONIA bid even if housing stays weak.

revised_trade.thesis: FACT: Housing turnover and prices are already contracting under current AONIA 4.35, AU employment fell 15.8k, unemployment rose to 4.5%, September consumer sentiment fell 5.2% to 84.4, and IB still prices a 4.94 area 2027 H1 terminal (~59bp over cash). INFERENCE: that residual hike path is a policy error into a housing bust and will be cut as labor/housing data stay weak; receiving the 2027 H1 AONIA strip is the cleanest slowdown expression. UNKNOWN: whether trimmed-mean 3.6%, the energy shock, or one more RBA hike lands before the housing channel dominates. Sidecar open_positions is empty, so this is a new OPEN versus the $100m cap, not an add to an existing IB position.
revised_trade.mispricing: IB 2027-06 at 4.94 (and 2027-03 at 4.86) still assumes roughly two additional 25bp RBA hikes after the housing, employment and sentiment evidence already in the packet. AU 2Y at 4.999 (99th percentile) is the sovereign echo of that same hike assumption; the tradable expression is AONIA IB, not the 2Y percentile. AUDUSD at 0.712 has not priced a domestic housing recession (76th 1y percentile, leveraged funds still adding AUD longs).
why_now: 16-Sep housing research (stamp duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, Sydney/Melbourne >7% off peak) is inside the freeze and has not been matched by a full IB-path unwind.
16-Sep Westpac-MI sentiment -5.2% to 84.4 is a fresh consumer-channel print after July spending had still been +1.1% m/m.
Fed hike and SOFR 3.85 plus BoJ 1.25% are supporting a USD/global-rates bid that is keeping AUD and AONIA from reflecting domestic slowdown.
Empty perma-bear book: funding vig is official SOFR 3.85 ACT/360 on the full $100m whether flat or not; the AONIA discrepancy is large enough versus that hurdle to deploy.

revised_trade.invalidation: Thesis fails if the 2027 H1 AONIA strip re-prices higher because the RBA delivers (or IB fully prices) the remaining ~50-60bp of tightening and the housing/labor channel stops deteriorating — specifically if employment and home-price declines reverse while trimmed-mean inflation reaccelerates or energy pass-through clearly lifts AU CPI. Do not invent a numeric stop; trusted marks stay on the locked IB strip.

Westpac-MI/consumer and RBA business-conditions updates after the September sentiment crash.
Energy/CPI surprises that either validate the hike path or, if they fade, unwind it.
principal_risks: AU inflation dashboard score remains 82; trimmed mean 3.6% y/y can still justify one or more hikes.
Desk thesis and energy-shock-absorber headlines: global tightening overlay can keep AONIA bid even with weak housing.
